breach.name: TelegramCombolists
breach.title: Combolists Posted to Telegram
breach.summary: In May 2024, 2B rows of data with 361M unique email addresses were collated from malicious Telegram channels. The data contained 122GB across 1.7k files with email addresses, usernames, passwords and in many cases, the website they were entered into. The data appears to have been sourced from a combination of existing combolists and info stealer malware.

background: In May 2024, 2B rows of data with 361M unique email addresses were collated from malicious Telegram channels . The data contained 122GB across 1.7k files with email addresses, usernames, passwords and in many cases, the website they were entered into. The data appears to have been sourced from a combination of existing combolists and info stealer malware.
how: The data appears to have been sourced from a combination of existing combolists and info stealer malware.
outcome: 361,468,099 accounts are listed in this breach. This is a count of accounts, not necessarily individual people.
The reported exposed data includes Email addresses, Passwords, Usernames.
editorial: The detail that sets this collection apart from an ordinary password dump is in the description: in many cases the records include the website the credentials were entered into . That turns a list of email-and-password pairs into a targeting list, an attacker no longer has to spray a credential across a hundred services hoping for a match, because the file already says where it worked.

The other half of the source is information-stealing malware, which changes what the data means for the person in it. Credentials harvested from an infected device were captured as they were typed. They can include accounts at sites that have never been breached, passwords created after every previous breach notification, and sessions from a browser's saved-password store in one sweep.

So the honest read of an appearance here is: your password is known, possibly with the site it belongs to, and possibly because a machine you used was compromised rather than a company you trusted. Clean the device first if there is any chance it was the source. Then rotate credentials in order of what they can unlock, email before everything, because email resets everything.

fields.name: Passwords
fields.why: Anyone reusing this password elsewhere has those accounts exposed too, credential stuffing is automated and tries them all within days.

fields.name: Email addresses
fields.why: The address becomes a confirmed, active target, expect more phishing, better aimed.

fields.name: Usernames
fields.why: A handle links this account to every other place the same handle is used.

actions: Change this password anywhere you reused it, starting with your email account, that is the one that can reset all the others.
Expect better-aimed phishing. A message that already knows your name and where you have an account is the whole point of a breach like this.
